reference: Bash type/help metadata and documented pre-socket parser/input rejection contracts. No matching GNU logger interface is claimed. Datagram wire values require an independent receiver or reviewed syscall mock in a future disposable VM.
coverage: Deferred: default and explicit wire formatting, tag and PID options.
Deferred: decimal, named, mixed and boundary priority parsing, aliases and invalid priorities.
Deferred: argument joining, -- handling, stdin framing, NUL rejection and message-size limits.
Deferred: private socket destination errors, path-length handling and truncation safety.
Deferred: close-on-exec, interrupted-send retry and cleanup on send failures using a syscall mock.
Runnable pre-socket priority/option/input rejection, including NUL and empty stdin; no datagram operation coverage.
exclusions: No datagram is sent and no socket destination is contacted. Successful priority/message formatting, delivery and descriptor behavior remain deferred for an independently reviewed socket mock or future disposable VM. GNU logger has a different CLI/protocol contract.

cases.purpose: Confirm Bash classifies the available bashlogger command as a builtin using the documented type -t contract, without invoking its logging operation.
Confirm help -s exposes the documented short synopsis. Expected text comes from the published bashlogger synopsis and Bash help -s formatting, not candidate output.

Check one datagram per valid call, default <13> user formatting, explicit tags and priorities, and the PID-bearing -i/--id form. Compute the expected PRI independently as facility * 8 + severity and compare exact packet bytes.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable VM with a private AF_UNIX receiver and an independently reviewed socket/syscall mock that prevents any host logging or network effects. Independently compute facility*8+severity, exact tag/PID bytes and one datagram per call.

cases.purpose: Check decimal PRI endpoints 0 and 191, named and numeric facility/severity pairs, case-insensitive names and documented aliases; verify invalid or out-of-range priorities fail before any datagram is sent.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable VM with a private AF_UNIX receiver and an independently reviewed socket/syscall mock that prevents any host logging or network effects. Exercise valid named, numeric and mixed priority forms and audit that invalid values open no socket; ordinary invalid-input rejection is covered separately.

cases.purpose: Check argument joining including empty arguments, -- termination, stdin input, removal of one trailing LF/CRLF, preservation of internal newlines, NUL rejection, and the documented 2047-byte message boundary against exact received bytes/status.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable VM with a private AF_UNIX receiver and an independently reviewed socket/syscall mock that prevents any host logging or network effects. Check exact packet bytes for argument joining, stdin newline framing and documented size boundaries; pre-socket NUL/empty rejection is covered separately.

cases.purpose: Check missing and non-socket destinations fail, an overlong socket path is rejected before send, and a path that would otherwise be truncated never receives a packet. Use only private relative fixture paths and independently inspect packet delivery/status.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable VM with a private AF_UNIX receiver and an independently reviewed socket/syscall mock that prevents any host logging or network effects. Use only relative private endpoints and a mock for socket/send/path-length outcomes; no real service endpoint may be used.

cases.purpose: Check SOCK_CLOEXEC/FD_CLOEXEC on the sending socket, no descriptor inheritance by an exec child, interrupted-send retry, and descriptor closure after one injected send failure or short send.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable VM with a private AF_UNIX receiver and an independently reviewed socket/syscall mock that prevents any host logging or network effects. Record CLOEXEC, closure and single-call EINTR/short-send/failure outcomes through the mock; no stress loop.
